- File: tests/test_review_apply_fixes_reviewer_manifest_validation.py
  Line or code reference: lines 119-130 (test_truncated_checksum_warns_but_passes)
  Problem: The test setup creates one truncated checksum (`_sha(files[0])[:40]` — 40 chars instead of 64), which the production code path at scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh:2202-2205 will count as a mismatch and increment `reviewer_checksum_mismatch_count`. The companion tests `test_garbled_checksum_warns_but_passes` (lines 99-116) and `test_every_checksum_wrong_is_summarised_once` (lines 133-142) were both updated in this PR to assert the new `EDITOR_REVIEWER_CHECKSUM_SUMMARY` warning, but this truncated test was not, even though it is the only test in the file that exercises a 40-character hash. The test name `test_truncated_checksum_warns_but_passes` also implies it verifies the warn path end-to-end, not just the per-file warning.
  Why it fails at runtime: A future regression that suppressed the summary emission when only one truncated hash was in play would still pass this test (the per-file `EDITOR_REVIEWER_CHECKSUM_UNVERIFIED` assertion only checks for the substring, not the absence of the summary), leaving the bug invisible until the next release-gate run. The four tests touching the warn path now diverge in coverage shape with no good reason.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4
- File: scripts/review_apply_fixes.sh
  Location: lines 2207-2209 (the new comment block above the summary emission)
  Issue: The comment "files_checked stops early when a missing entry fails the attempt" describes behaviour that is technically correct but easy to misread. The counter `reviewer_manifest_file_count` is incremented at the top of each loop iteration (line 2140) BEFORE the audit-validation break (line 2166) or processed-entry break (line 2200) can fire, so `files_checked` reflects "files iterated up to and including the one that triggered the break" — not "files in the full manifest minus those skipped". A reader seeing `files_checked=2` cannot tell whether the manifest had 2 entries or 3+ from this comment alone.
  Suggested minimal fix: tighten the comment to spell out the semantics, e.g. "files_checked counts every manifest line iterated before the loop exited — including the one that triggered the break — so a value smaller than the manifest size means the attempt failed on a missing entry or audit bullet."
  Estimated lines changed: 2-3 lines (comment only).
  HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1
